blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A maximization search holds an incumbent worth 3,200. Four solved nodes report: A, LP 3,180, fractional; B, LP infeasible; C, LP 3,240, all 0 and 1; D, LP 3,260, fractional. Which of them are branched on?

options.text: A and D, since each still has a fractional variable
options.says: A's bound, 3,180, is below the incumbent's 3,200, so nothing under A can win; it is pruned by bound.

options.text: D only, since A cannot win and B and C are leaves
options.says: Right: B is infeasible, C is integral (and becomes the incumbent at 3,240), A cannot beat 3,200, and D can still beat 3,240.

options.text: C and D, since both of them are above 3,200
options.says: C's LP solution is a real plan and the best one in C, so it is a leaf; there is nothing to split.

options.text: All four, since no plan is proven best yet
options.says: A node is pruned when it is infeasible, integral, or cannot beat the incumbent, proof or no proof.

origin.section: Prune a Node That Is Infeasible, Integral, or Cannot Beat the Incumbent

questions.stem: Midway through a maximization search, the incumbent is worth 9,400 and three nodes wait, carrying bounds 9,700, 9,520 and 9,380. What range must the optimum lie in?

options.text: From 9,380 to 9,700, the lowest and highest of the node bounds
options.says: The incumbent is a real plan worth 9,400, so the optimum is at least 9,400.

options.text: From 9,400 to 9,520, since the 9,700 bound tends to be loose
options.says: The node with bound 9,700 is not ruled out, so plans worth up to 9,700 may still exist below it.

options.text: Exactly 9,400, since the search keeps the plan it has found
options.says: The incumbent is only proven best when no waiting bound is above it; here two are.

options.text: From 9,400 to 9,700, the best plan so far and the top bound
options.says: Right: the incumbent is a lower bound and every unexplored plan is below some waiting bound, the largest being 9,700.

origin.section: The Optimum Always Lies Between the Incumbent and the Best Waiting Bound

questions.stem: Every plan's value is a whole number of $k. The incumbent is worth 5,120, and a node's LP value is 5,120.8 with one fractional variable. What happens to the node?

options.text: It is branched on, since 5,120.8 is above the incumbent's 5,120
options.says: No plan below the node can be worth 5,120.8; the best whole value it allows is 5,120, which only ties.

options.text: It is rounded up to 5,121 and branched on, since bounds round up
options.says: A bound is rounded down: the largest whole number not above 5,120.8 is 5,120.

options.text: It is pruned, since no plan below it can do better than a tie
options.says: Right: floor(5,120.8) = 5,120 is not above the incumbent, and a tie is no improvement.

options.text: It becomes the incumbent, since 5,120.8 beats every plan so far
options.says: A fractional LP solution is not a plan, so it can never become the incumbent.

origin.section: With Whole-Number Values, Round the Bound Down Before Comparing

concepts: which solved nodes still need splitting
the interval that must hold the optimum midway through a search
a node just above the incumbent when plan values are whole numbers
